Land status and neighbourhoods: the Nation describes 10 reserves totalling about 2,930 ha, within a Traditional Territory of approximately 780,000 hectares. The Community Housing Plan names four neighbourhoods within the reserve lands: Mount Currie Village (IR 1 and IR 10), the centre with the administrative and civic facilities; Xet̓ólacw Village (IR 6), also called the Upper Community, the largest residential neighbourhood; Lillooet Lake Road (IR 3 and IR 8); and Kwetsa7 (IR 2), the last two less developed and rural residential in character. The surrounding unincorporated Pemberton Valley (off reserve) is Squamish-Lillooet Regional District (SLRD) Electoral Area C. Statistics Canada treats "Mount Currie" as an Indian reserve census subdivision (code 5931843) within the SLRD; the 2021 Census counted 1,240 people in private households there, median age 33.2 years.
This guide covers Mount Currie's condo buildings, townhome complexes and land: what each source verifies, the local rules, and what buyers ask.
Condo buildings in Mount Currie

Mount Currie is the main community of the Líl̓wat Nation, on federal reserve lands. There is no open-market housing of any kind here — no condos, no strata, no fee-simple sales; housing is allocated through the Nation for its citizens. The surrounding off-reserve frame (SLRD Electoral Area C) is given in as surrounding-area context only, labelled as such.
Streets, schools and transit near Mount Currie condos

items.t: Mount Currie sits in the Pemberton Valley approximately 160 km north of Vancouver and approximately 35 km north of Whistler via Highway 99 (the Sea-to-Sky Highway), and is also approachable via the Duffy Lake Road (Highway 99 east). The Village of Pemberton is the neighbouring municipality a few kilometres west. The Nation states the community is home to approximately 1,495 of its more than 2,275 citizens, and is named for Mount Currie, the 2,591 m (8,501 ft) mountain at the centre of Líl̓wat Traditional Territory.

Land status and neighbourhoods: the Nation describes 10 reserves totalling about 2,930 ha, within a Traditional Territory of approximately 780,000 hectares. The Community Housing Plan names four neighbourhoods within the reserve lands: Mount Currie Village (IR 1 and IR 10), the centre with the administrative and civic facilities; Xet̓ólacw Village (IR 6), also called the Upper Community, the largest residential neighbourhood; Lillooet Lake Road (IR 3 and IR 8); and Kwetsa7 (IR 2), the last two less developed and rural residential in character. The surrounding unincorporated Pemberton Valley (off reserve) is Squamish-Lillooet Regional District (SLRD) Electoral Area C. Statistics Canada treats "Mount Currie" as an Indian reserve census subdivision (code 5931843) within the SLRD; the 2021 Census counted 1,240 people in private households there, median age 33.2 years.

Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere — there is none, by the nature of the ground. The community's housing is single-detached family homes in the village neighbourhoods, including newer subdivision homes and modular/manufactured homes built to CSA Z-240, allocated through the Nation.

Schools: Xet̓ólacw Community School is the Nation's own school in the Xet̓ólacw community; under the Local Education Agreement with School District 48 (Sea to Sky), Líl̓wat students also attend Signal Hill Elementary and Pemberton Secondary School in Pemberton, and SD48's Bus 5 route runs "Owl Ridge, Reid Rd & Mt. Currie" to those schools, stopping at IR 10 Road and Spirit Circle on Pemberton Portage Road. Ts̓zil Learning Centre, 125 Lillooet Lake Road, is the Nation's learning centre (adult education, Ucwalmícwts language, history and culture, carpentry and other vocational training in partnership with Capilano University), in a 22,000 sq ft facility opened fall 2018.

Transit and the community core: BC Transit's Pemberton Valley Transit is cost-shared between BC Transit, the Village of Pemberton, the SLRD and Líl̓wat Nation; local service connects Xit'olacw and Mt Currie to the Village of Pemberton, and a commuter service runs between Pemberton and Whistler. The Nation is redeveloping its commercial core in Mount Currie (gas station/convenience store, 12-unit motel, plans for a permanent artisan's market); Úll̓us, the administrative building a block off Main Street, includes a gym, banquet hall and Neighbourhood House.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Mount Currie

items.t: How ownership actually works here (the operative frame): the Nation's published "Five Steps to Home Ownership on Reserve" — (1) meet the Housing Manager; (2) a land encumbrance check from the Lands Department confirming a serviced lot is available and registered to the person; (3) a Band Council Resolution (the Band Council acts as guarantor on the loan); (4) possible housing subsidies from Indigenous Services Canada; (5) a Ministerial Loan Guarantee and bank financing. Because the Council acts as guarantor and a Ministerial Loan Guarantee backs the loan, standard mortgage and foreclosure mechanics do not apply the way they do off reserve. The Nation's own building-cost guidance: modest new construction at about $250–$300 per square foot including water, sewer and hydro connections, and CSA Z-240 modular/pre-manufactured homes at about $160–$180 per square foot installed and hooked up, with Mount Currie modulars required to meet zone 6 construction standards and a roof snow load rating of 136 lb per square foot.

Form B — does not exist here: Off reserve, Strata Property Act s. 59 requires a strata to provide a Form B Information Certificate on a resale (fees, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary, depreciation report attached; within 7 days; max $35 + 25¢/page). There is no strata and no resale market in Mount Currie, so there is no Form B to request; the equivalent diligence for a citizen is the Lands Department land encumbrance check in the five-step process above.

Depreciation reports and CRF — provincial strata rules, no strata to apply them to: Off reserve, stratas with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years (since July 1, 2024) and contribute at least 10% of the operating fund to the CRF (since November 1, 2023). Neither obligation creates or describes any housing right on reserve land, where capital planning runs through the Nation's Housing Plan (2018–2033) and its 12-units-per-year build goal.

Rental and age bylaws — provincial strata law, stated for comparison only: Off reserve, strata rental-restriction bylaws are void since November 24, 2022, and Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 allow only a 55-or-older residency bylaw (Regulation 7.01 exemptions: legacy residents, live-in caregivers, and from May 1, 2023 younger spouses/partners and defined children). Mount Currie has no strata corporations, so no strata age bylaw creates a 55+ product here and no rental-bylaw rule creates a rental right here; rental housing in the community is Nation-administered band housing.

Surrounding-area frame — SLRD Electoral Area C (context only, does not govern reserve parcels): Off reserve, the Pemberton Valley around Mount Currie is SLRD Electoral Area C, a separate jurisdiction with its own bylaws; the Village of Pemberton is the neighbouring municipality with standard municipal taxes, zoning and MLS sales.

Taxes and transfer taxes — do not apply as they do off reserve: Standard municipal and regional district property taxes, and provincial property transfer tax, do not apply to reserve land the way they apply to fee-simple land off reserve. For completeness, the off-reserve BC PTT rates are 1% on the first $200,000, 2% to $2M, 3% above, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3M — they do not price a reserve-land home.

GST and buyer programs — off-reserve instruments, no application here: 21) and trust deposits (s. 18), the $60,000 Home Buyers' Plan, the FHSA ($40,000 lifetime / $8,000 per year) and CMHC premiums of 0.60%–4.50%). None of these is a route into Mount Currie housing: there is no developer sale, no presale and no MLS purchase for them to attach to. Financing for citizens runs through the Band Council Resolution / Ministerial Loan Guarantee process above.

items.t: Housing demand here is the opposite of a retirement market. The Community Housing Plan's priority order — families with young children first, multi-generational families second, Elders third, singles and couples fourth, with rent-to-own and help building their own homes as the priority tenures — is the community's own stated position. Any page framing Mount Currie as a retirement or lifestyle destination inverts it.

The Nation renamed itself in living memory. The name Mount Currie Band was officially changed to Líl̓wat Nation on September 12, 2014 (Nation's 2014 annual report) — older documents using "Mount Currie Indian Band" refer to the same Nation.

The Nation is one of the community's largest employers. Through its governance, corporations and businesses, the Nation provides employment for more than 400 community members — the economic base of the community is the Nation itself, not a commuter, second-home or retiree market.

The build goal is 12 units per year in both the Mount Currie and Xet̓ólacw communities under the Community Housing Plan (2018–2033), allocated to citizens — which is why "new development" and "presale" language never applies here, and why REDMA has nothing to attach to.

The mountain the town is named for is the territory's centrepiece: Mount Currie, 2,591 m (8,501 ft), at the centre of a Traditional Territory of approximately 780,000 hectares — against reserve lands of about 2,930 ha in 10 reserves. The reserve land base is a small fraction of the territory, which is the land context behind the Nation-administered housing system.

items.t: Mount Currie is the main community of the Líl̓wat Nation (Ucwalmícwts-speaking; the band was formerly styled the Mount Currie Indian Band). The Nation states the community is home to approximately 1,495 of its more than 2,275 citizens, and is named for Mount Currie, the 2,591 m (8,501 ft) mountain at the centre of Líl̓wat Traditional Territory.

Land status: the community sits on Líl̓wat reserve lands — the Nation describes 10 reserves totalling about 2,930 ha, a small fraction of a Traditional Territory of approximately 780,000 hectares extending north to Gates Lake, east to the Upper Stein Valley and west to the coastal inlets. Reserve lands are federal lands set aside for the Nation; they are not a municipality, and the surrounding unincorporated Pemberton Valley is Squamish-Lillooet Regional District (SLRD) Electoral Area C. Statistics Canada treats "Mount Currie" as an Indian reserve census subdivision (code 5931843) within the Squamish-Lillooet Regional District.

Neighbourhoods within the reserve lands (per the Nation's Community Housing Plan): Mount Currie Village (IR 1 and IR 10), the centre with the administrative and civic facilities; Xet̓ólacw Village (IR 6), also called the Upper Community, the largest residential neighbourhood; Lillooet Lake Road (IR 3 and IR 8); and Kwetsa7 (IR 2), the last two less developed and rural residential in character.

Location: approximately 160 km north of Vancouver and approximately 35 km north of Whistler via the Sea-to-Sky Highway (Highway 99), also approachable via the Duffy Lake Road (Highway 99 east). The Village of Pemberton is the neighbouring municipality a few kilometres west.

Population (census): the 2021 Census Indigenous Population Profile for the Mount Currie census subdivision counts 1,240 people in private households (25% sample data), median age 33.2 years; the Nation's own figure for citizens living in the community is approximately 1,495.

Transit: BC Transit's Pemberton Valley Transit is cost-shared between BC Transit, the Village of Pemberton, the SLRD and Líl̓wat Nation; local service within Pemberton connects the communities of Xit'olacw and Mt Currie to the Village, and a separate commuter service runs between Pemberton and Whistler.

Community core: the Nation is redeveloping its commercial core in Mount Currie, which includes a gas station/convenience store and a 12-unit motel, with plans for a permanent artisan's market; Úll̓us, the Nation's administrative building a block off Main Street, includes a gym, banquet hall and Neighbourhood House and houses the Infrastructure Department; the Nation, through its governance, corporations and businesses, provides employment for more than 400 community members. The nearest full-service grocery and retail centre is the Village of Pemberton.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Mount Currie

items.t: On-reserve housing process (the regime that actually applies): home ownership for Líl̓wat citizens runs through the Nation's five steps — Housing Manager first, then the Lands Department land encumbrance check, Band Council Resolution (the Council acts as guarantor), Indigenous Services Canada subsidy and Ministerial Loan Guarantee checks, then a lender. Because the Band Council acts as guarantor and a Ministerial Loan Guarantee backs the loan, standard mortgage and foreclosure mechanics do not apply the way they do off reserve.

No strata frame on this area: there is no strata corporation, no Form B (Strata Property Act s. 59 does not attach to reserve-land housing), no strata fees, no CRF and no depreciation report for any home in this community. None of that creates any right or product in Mount Currie itself.

Land use: there is no municipal zoning bylaw for the reserve lands — land allocation runs through the Nation's Lands Department and Band Council processes. The surrounding off-reserve valley is SLRD Electoral Area C and the Village of Pemberton's rules govern Pemberton land only; no SLRD or Pemberton bylaw number is carried for the reserve lands, and none applies to them.

Property taxes / levies: For that reason no PTT calculation, tax due date or penalty schedule is stated for Mount Currie itself; the standard BC figures in the next bullet are the off-reserve comparison frame only.

Taxes and rebates (off-reserve comparison frame only — e.g., a Pemberton purchase): PTT is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2 million, 3% above $2 million, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3 million; a page row reading "Over $3M — 5%" is a compression of the 3% tier plus that further 2% — the tier math governs. Exemptions: first-time buyers — exempt on the first $500,000 at fair market value $835,000 or less, partial to $860,000; newly built home exemption — full to $1,100,000, eliminated at $1,150,000. FTHB GST rebate — Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122 (100% of GST to $1M, maximum $50,000, phasing to $1.5M, agreements Mar 20, 2025–2031); New Housing Rebate 36% / maximum $6,300 / $350K–$450K; HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 lifetime / $8,000 per year; CMHC premiums 0.6%–4.5%. 5% GST applies to new construction, not resales.

blocks.text: Good to know about Mount Currie townhomes

items.t: The mountain is the address, not the market. "Mount Currie" names the 2,591 m mountain at the centre of Líl̓wat Traditional Territory, the Nation's main community beneath it — and, confusingly, a Pemberton manufactured-home park's view branding ("Mt. Currie View Village"). Only the middle one is this area, and it is the one with nothing for sale.

A 780,000-hectare territory, 2,930 hectares of reserve. The Nation's reserves are a small fraction of its Traditional Territory (north to Gates Lake, east to the Upper Stein Valley, west to the coastal inlets) — the reserve-land tenure that governs housing here is a product of that history, not a zoning choice.

The guarantor is the government. On-reserve financing works because the Band Council itself acts as guarantor and a Ministerial Loan Guarantee backs the loan — a structure with no equivalent in a strata or fee-simple purchase, and the reason foreclosure mechanics differ here.

Snow load is a build specification, not a weather remark. Modular homes for Mount Currie must meet zone 6 construction standards with a roof snow load rating of 136 lb per square foot, per the Nation's own home-ownership material — a Pemberton-valley build standard a southern buyer would never think to ask about.

The learning centre is a university partnership on reserve. Ts̓zil Learning Centre (125 Lillooet Lake Road) delivers Capilano University-partnered programs — Ucwalmícwts language, history and culture, carpentry and vocational training — from a 22,000 sq ft facility opened in fall 2018.

The Community Housing Plan allocates new homes to families with young children first, then multi-generational families, with Elders third — a Nation policy order that replaces any notion of a waitlist a buyer could join from outside.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Mount Currie
What trades here

items.t: What a "lot" means here — the Nation's allocation system, documented as the land system itself: a citizen's path runs through the Nation's "Five Steps to Home Ownership on Reserve" — (1) meet the Housing Manager; (2) a land encumbrance check from the Lands Department confirming a serviced lot is available and registered to the person; (3) a Band Council Resolution (the Band Council acts as guarantor on the loan); (4) possible housing subsidies from Indigenous Services Canada; (5) a Ministerial Loan Guarantee and bank financing. The serviced lot is allocated and registered through that process — it is never listed, priced or sold on an open market.

Tenure: neither freehold nor strata — Nation-administered housing on reserve land (band housing, and member home ownership through the process above). Fee-simple lots as a default form do not exist on this area, and bare-land strata as a form does not exist here either: there is no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees and no depreciation report for any home in this community.

Housing form on the allocated lots: single-detached family homes in the village neighbourhoods (Mount Currie Village IR 1/IR 10, Xet̓ólacw IR 6, Lillooet Lake Road IR 3/IR 8, Kwetsa7 IR 2), including newer subdivision homes and modular/manufactured homes built to CSA Z-240. The Nation's own building-cost guidance: modest new construction at about $250–$300 per square foot including water, sewer and hydro connections, and CSA Z-240 modular/pre-manufactured homes at about $160–$180 per square foot installed and hooked up, with Mount Currie modulars required to meet zone 6 construction standards and a roof snow load rating of 136 lb per square foot.

The Nation is building new housing in both the Mount Currie and Xet̓ólacw communities, with a goal of 12 units per year under the Community Housing Plan (2018–2033), allocated to citizens under the Plan's priority order (families with young children first, then multi-generational families, Elders third, then singles and couples). "New development" and presale marketing language never applies to it.

Different municipality, manufactured-home form, pad-rental tenure: three independent reasons it is not Mount Currie land. A manufactured home on a rented pad is not lot stock and not land ownership in any event, and no pad-rent dollar figure is published here.

Tenure record only: the reserve-land tenure itself is the record to name for any listing or lead implying otherwise — reserve land is federal land set aside for the Nation, administered by the Nation; it is not corporation-share, undivided-interest, leasehold, co-op, life-lease or pad-rental tenure, and a non-member acquires no interest at all. Inquiries go to the Líl̓wat Nation (info@lilwat.ca, 604-894-6115, per the Nation's published contact information).
Any parcel question goes to the Nation's Lands Department.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Mount Currie

items.t: Land use — no municipal zoning bylaw for the reserve lands: land allocation runs through the Nation's Lands Department and Band Council processes. The surrounding off-reserve valley is SLRD Electoral Area C and the Village of Pemberton's bylaws govern Pemberton land only — no SLRD or Pemberton bylaw number is carried for the reserve lands, and none applies to them; no Pemberton village or District bylaw is imported here.

Subdivision — the provincial subdivision frame does not run here: Off-reserve bylaw numbers from other jurisdictions (e.g., Surrey 8830, Vancouver 5208) govern their own municipalities only and are never carried onto reserve land.

Because the Band Council acts as guarantor and a Ministerial Loan Guarantee backs the loan, standard mortgage and foreclosure mechanics do not apply the way they do off reserve — the lender's security runs through the Nation's process, not against fee-simple title. The off-reserve court-foreclosure frame (Rules 21-7/13-5, PD-66, Form 60) does not apply here.
Property taxes / transfer taxes — do not apply as they do off reserve: For that reason no tax due date, penalty schedule or PTT calculation is stated for Mount Currie itself.

Taxes and rebates (off-reserve comparison frame only — e.g., a Pemberton purchase): PTT tiers 1% to $200,000, 2% to $2,000,000, 3% above, plus a further 2% on the residential portion over $3,000,000 — on a $900,000 off-reserve purchase (round illustration only), fully residential, no exemption: $2,000 + $14,000 = $16,000. (Reference: $3.5M → $93,000 INCLUDING the further 2% tier.) FTHB GST rebate — new HOUSING, not bare land: Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026, CRA governs; 100% to $1M phasing to $1.5M, max $50,000, agreements Mar 20, 2025–2031. New Housing Rebate 36% / max $6,300 / $350K–$450K; HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 / $8,000 per year.
GST on vacant land — CRA GI-003 level only, off-reserve frame: developer/business sales and newly subdivided lots generally TAXABLE; an individual's personal-use land generally exempt.

Strata block — stated for comparison, no application here: off reserve, a bare-land strata lot carries Form B (within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page), depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for 5+ lots since July 1, 2024, a minimum 10% CRF since November 1, 2023, void rental bylaws since November 24, 2022, and only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). None of that creates or describes any right on reserve land, where there are no strata corporations.

Manufactured homes and pad rent (MHPTA frame): the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act limits pad-rent increases in manufactured home parks (2026: 2.3% plus a proportional amount; 2027: 2.2% plus a proportional amount — Act percentages only; no pad-rent dollar figure is published here, ever).

faq.q: Can anyone buy a condo — or any home — in Mount Currie?
faq.a: No. Mount Currie is the main community of the Líl̓wat Nation on reserve land; housing is allocated and financed through the Nation's own process for its citizens, starting with the Nation's Housing Manager and Lands Department — there is no fee-simple open market and no condo product of any kind. Inquiries go to the Líl̓wat Nation (info@lilwat.ca, 604-894-6115).

faq.q: Why doesn't the BC condo/strata system apply here?
faq.a: Because the land is federal reserve land administered by the Nation, not provincial fee-simple land: there is no strata corporation, no Form B, no depreciation-report or CRF regime, and no municipal zoning bylaw for the reserve lands. Land allocation runs through the Nation's Lands Department and Band Council.

faq.q: How does home ownership work for Líl̓wat citizens?
faq.a: Through the Nation's five steps: meet the Housing Manager; get a land encumbrance check from the Lands Department confirming a serviced lot registered to you; obtain a Band Council Resolution (the Council acts as guarantor); check Indigenous Services Canada housing subsidies and the Ministerial Loan Guarantee; and arrange bank financing.

faq.q: Is Mount Currie a retirement destination?
faq.a: The census subdivision's median age is 33.2 years, and members surveyed for the Community Housing Plan ranked housing for families with young children as the top priority, followed by multi-generational families, Elders third, and singles and couples — with rent-to-own and help building their own homes as the priority tenures.

faq.q: If I want to buy near Mount Currie, where do I actually look?
faq.a: The Village of Pemberton, a few kilometres west: fee-simple homes in a municipality with standard taxes and MLS sales — a completely different tenure from Mount Currie.

faq.q: Are there any townhouses in Mount Currie?
faq.a: None — 0 strata, 0 fee-simple, 0 presales, and the zero is structural: the land is Líl̓wat reserve land, where tenure is neither freehold nor strata and housing runs through the Nation for its citizens. There is no townhouse market here to search.

faq.q: Can anyone buy a house in Mount Currie?
faq.a: No. Housing is allocated and financed through the Líl̓wat Nation's own process for its citizens, starting with the Nation's Housing Manager and Lands Department — there is no fee-simple open market. Inquiries go to the Nation (info@lilwat.ca, 604-894-6115).

faq.q: How does home ownership work for Líl̓wat citizens?
faq.a: Through the Nation's five steps: meet the Housing Manager; get a Lands Department land encumbrance check confirming a serviced lot registered to you; obtain a Band Council Resolution (the Council acts as guarantor); check Indigenous Services Canada housing subsidies and the Ministerial Loan Guarantee; then arrange bank financing. Standard mortgage and foreclosure mechanics do not apply the way they do off reserve.

faq.q: Can anyone buy a house — or a half duplex — in Mount Currie?
faq.a: No. Mount Currie is the main community of the Líl̓wat Nation on reserve land; housing is allocated and financed through the Nation's own process for its citizens — there is no fee-simple open market, and therefore no duplex or half duplex for a general buyer to purchase. Inquiries go to the Líl̓wat Nation (info@lilwat.ca, 604-894-6115).

faq.q: Is Mount Currie housing freehold or strata?
faq.a: Neither — directly: Nation-administered housing on reserve land. Mount Currie housing is not freehold or strata.

faq.q: What does it cost to build a home there?
faq.a: The Nation's own guidance: New construction of a modest home at about $250–$300 per square foot including water, sewer and hydro connections, and modular/pre-manufactured homes built to CSA Z-240 at about $160–$180 per square foot installed and hooked up; modulars for Mount Currie must meet zone 6 construction standards and a roof snow load rating of 136 lb per square foot.
